source.title: Can quantised autoencoders find and interpret circuits in language models?

record.tranche_reason: The post applies a different circuit-finding approach to GPT-2 Small IOI and uses activation patching with a logit-difference measure to examine the role of a recovered component. It reports partial alignment with the original circuit and differences across corrupted prompt conditions.
record.gate_note: The decision-tree accuracies, PCA separation, code frequencies, and hyperparameter results characterize the post's learned representations or classifier; they do not directly measure the circuit's effect on IOI behavior. The continuous-residual decision tree is described as finding a different circuit, but no component-level behavioral outcome is reported for it.
record.test_reason: A different, unsupervised circuit-finding method (VQ-VAE codes plus decision trees) is applied to GPT-2 small IOI. The post compares the recovered attention layers with the original circuit and checks attention layer 8 by activation patching. Its results bear on V4 (method-independence) and, at layer level, on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that the unsupervised VQ-VAE plus decision-tree method recovered attention layers containing several original IOI components: S-inhibition (layers 7 and 8), duplicate-token (layers 0 and 3) and previous-token (layer 2). It missed induction and backup name movers, which the author attributes to its one-input, one-output structure. Patching suggests attention layer 8 does S-inhibition. A decision tree on continuous residual streams found a quite different, less aligned circuit.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GPT-2 Small IOI and activation patching with a logit-difference measure, but identifies components using VQ-VAE codes and decision trees and tests residual streams at the attention-layer level rather than testing the original head-level circuit and its full faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported relative importance of attention layer 8 changes between the switched-name corrupted prompts and the counterexamples where the third name is neither of the first two.
record.problems: The activation-patching analysis uses only 8 tutorial prompts. The author says the logit-difference comparison is hacky, gives no numerical patching values or uncertainty, and describes the S-inhibition interpretation as circumstantial. The analysis identifies layers rather than individual heads and does not test full-circuit faithfulness or completeness.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for classifier accuracies, PCA, code frequencies, or hyperparameter results because these measure representation/classifier properties rather than the circuit's effect on IOI behavior. The continuous-residual decision-tree result is described as a different circuit but has no reported component-level behavioral outcome.

untested.parts: Head-level identity of the 26 heads and 7 classes; faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
All of it. No ablation of name movers or self-repair test; the method simply missed the backup name-mover layers.
All of it. Only GPT-2 small is used.
Ablation types, alternative metrics, and quantified faithfulness or completeness.
All of it. No templates, name orders or name counts are tested as IOI variants.

missing.what: Layers in the discrete-code circuit compared with the original IOI circuit: attention layers 0/embed, 2, 3, 7 and 8 matched; no MLPs; induction and backup name-mover layers missed; 6 of 6 layers contain original heads (chance about 0.02%).
missing.locator: Code circuit analysis, comparison with original IOI paper

missing.what: Continuous-residual decision-tree circuit is quite different from the discrete-code circuit and less aligned with the original layers.
missing.locator: Extending on the decision tree as a circuit-finder

record.verdict_notes: The study is mainly a method comparison, so V4 is the version most directly tested, and the reader wrongly marked V4 not_tested. The reader's V6 links are wrong because the corrupted prompts are patching baselines. Evidence quality is weak: 8 prompts, no numbers, layer-level only, and the circuit-comparison figures are not available in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the full 26-head, 7-class circuit or the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. Its interpretation is at the attention-layer level, not the individual-head level.

The post does not systematically compare other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics. It describes a continuous-residual decision-tree result as different, but does not report a component-level behavioral test for that circuit.
It compares two corrupted-prompt conditions, but does not compare ablation types or alternative metrics, nor directly quantify the completeness or faithfulness of the recovered circuit.

The post considers two corrupted-prompt conditions, including prompts with switched name order, but does not test generalization across templates or more names, or establish that the entire circuit carries IOI in those settings.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.size_stated: 768 model dimension; 13 layers (26 if split into attention and MLP blocks)
rows.operation_detail: Patched residual streams after attention blocks using clean activations on corrupted prompts; measured the logit difference between the subject and indirect-object names.

conditions.value: 8 IOI prompts from the TransformerLens IOI analysis tutorial

rows.measure: Contribution to the subject-versus-indirect-object logit difference
rows.value: Attention layer 8 had the largest positive contribution; numerical value not stated
rows.locator: Code circuit analysis; activation-patching plot and accompanying text
rows.note: The author relates layer 8 to S-inhibition, but says the interpretation is circumstantial and does not isolate individual heads.
rows.check: This row is about the role of layer-8 components, so it bears on V1. It does not bear on V6: the switched-name prompt is the corruption baseline for patching, not a prompt variant on which the circuit is tested. The evidence is layer-level only, with no numbers, so it is partial for the head-level claim.

source_check.correct: For V1, state=cannot_determine. Layer-8 residual-stream patching establishes a contribution, but does not isolate the claimed heads or evaluate the circuit's faithfulness, completeness and minimality.
source_check.problem: Partial measurement coverage does not demonstrate that V1's effect appears incompletely; the S-inhibition interpretation is explicitly circumstantial.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.size_stated: 768 model dimension; 13 layers (26 if split into attention and MLP blocks)
rows.operation_detail: Compared layer importance from activation patching on the original corrupted prompts with importance on the post's closer counterexamples.

conditions.value: IOI prompts and counterexamples where the third name is neither of the first two
counterexamples that do not require S-inhibition

rows.measure: Difference in layer importance for the subject-versus-indirect-object logit difference
rows.baseline: Importance from patching with the original corrupted prompts
rows.value: Attention layer 8 had the highest difference; the author says it mattered in both conditions but mattered most when the corrupted examples did not require S-inhibition; numerical values not stated
rows.note: The comparison indicates prompt-condition sensitivity, but does not establish that the full circuit carries IOI across prompt variants.
rows.check: Remove V6, since the counterexamples are an alternative corruption distribution, not an IOI prompt variant. The row shows layer-8 importance changing with the corrupted-prompt choice, which is weak evidence of V5-type sensitivity. No values are given and the metric is admittedly hacky.

source_check.correct: State=cannot_determine for V1; state=observed for V5's corruption-distribution sensitivity. Layer 8 matters under both corruptions and has the highest importance difference, with greater importance for third-name counterexamples.
source_check.problem: The shared partial state conflates unverified head-level mechanism with explicitly observed qualitative corruption sensitivity.
